intended_object: The closed (monothetic) subgroup generated by an element x of a topological group G: the closure of the cyclic subgroup ⟨x⟩ = {xⁿ : n ∈ ℤ}, i.e. the smallest closed subgroup containing x. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition is `(Subgroup.zpowers x).topologicalClosure`. That is the topological closure of the cyclic subgroup generated by `x`, packaged as a subgroup. By `Subgroup.topologicalClosure_minimal`, this is the smallest closed subgroup containing `x`, which is the standard object. The setting (a group with a topological space and `IsTopologicalGroup`) is exactly the setting in which Mathlib defines `Subgroup.topologicalClosure`, so the definition is not too narrow. Searching Mathlib for `closedZpowers`, "procyclic" and "monothetic" found no dedicated declaration for this object; it is only the composite of two Mathlib constructions. The one gap is that no additive version is generated via `to_additive`. That is a convenience issue and does not affect whether this definition is faithful.
